brief: Meta's Muse signals agentic AI going mass-market. GS's Rich Privorotsky expects more such products as corporates provide safety, infrastructure and distribution, and sees the aggregate impact as positive for equities and structurally disinflationary. GS argues the original AI infrastructure trade is still cheap: hyperscaler earnings have caught up with performance while the median AI infrastructure stock has de-rated from 32x forward earnings in April to 22x today. DB's Jim Reid says a powerful global capex cycle, driven by AI and government strategic-autonomy spending, is the growth 'superglue' explaining surging yields alongside record-high equities, tight credit spreads and subdued cross-asset vol. DB estimates the cycle could run five years and add 3-6% cumulatively to GDP. On ROIC, GS's Eric Sheridan estimates Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle and SpaceX need $1.42 trillion combined revenue in 2028-30 to earn 15% ROIC on their 2026-27 AI capex. Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet already hold a $1.69 trillion backlog and need to convert only about 59% of it to clear that hurdle. Hyperscaler CDS spreads have widened relative to QQQ put vol, so credit is pricing more AI stress than equity options. The desk's call: run AI longs hedged with cheap QQQ puts.
